meta.subject: math
meta.description: Geometry facts: area, perimeter, volume, angles, Pythagorean theorem, circles, polygons, transformations, coordinate geometry, trigonometry basics

facts.statement: Area of a rectangle = length x width
Perimeter of a rectangle = 2(length + width)
Area of a triangle = (1/2) x base x height
Area of a circle = pi x radius squared (pi x r^2)
Circumference of a circle = 2 x pi x radius = pi x diameter
Area of a parallelogram = base x height (height is perpendicular to the base)
Area of a trapezoid = (1/2)(base1 + base2) x height
Pi (approximately 3.14159) is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter
Area is measured in square units (sq cm, sq m, sq ft); perimeter is measured in linear units (cm, m, ft)
Area of a square = side x side = side^2
Perimeter of a square = 4 x side
Area of a rhombus = (1/2) x diagonal1 x diagonal2
Area of a kite = (1/2) x diagonal1 x diagonal2
Area of a regular polygon = (1/2) x apothem x perimeter
Heron's formula: area of triangle with sides a, b, c is sqrt(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)) where s = (a+b+c)/2
A sector area = (angle/360) x pi x r^2; arc length = (angle/360) x 2 x pi x r

common_errors.wrong: area of a triangle is base times height
common_errors.correct: Area of a triangle is HALF of base times height: (1/2) x base x height.

common_errors.wrong: the height of a triangle is always one of its sides
common_errors.correct: The height is the perpendicular distance from the base to the opposite vertex, which may or may not coincide with a side.

common_errors.wrong: circumference equals pi times radius
common_errors.correct: Circumference = 2 x pi x radius (or pi x diameter). Using just pi x radius gives half the circumference.

common_errors.wrong: doubling the radius doubles the area of a circle
common_errors.correct: Doubling the radius quadruples the area: pi(2r)^2 = 4 pi r^2.

common_errors.wrong: perimeter and area use the same units
common_errors.correct: Perimeter uses linear units (cm, m); area uses square units (cm^2, m^2).

facts.statement: A right angle measures exactly 90 degrees
An acute angle measures less than 90 degrees
An obtuse angle measures more than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees
A straight angle measures exactly 180 degrees
Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees
Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees
Vertical angles (formed by two intersecting lines) are always equal
The sum of the interior angles of any triangle is 180 degrees
The sum of the interior angles of a polygon with n sides is (n-2) x 180 degrees
A reflex angle measures more than 180 degrees but less than 360 degrees
Adjacent angles share a common side and vertex
When a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are equal
When a transversal crosses parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal
When a transversal crosses parallel lines, co-interior (same-side interior) angles are supplementary (add to 180)
An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles
Each interior angle of a regular polygon with n sides = (n-2) x 180 / n
The sum of exterior angles of any convex polygon is always 360 degrees

common_errors.wrong: complementary angles add to 180 degrees
common_errors.correct: Complementary angles add to 90 degrees. Supplementary angles add to 180 degrees.

common_errors.wrong: the angles of a triangle can add up to more than 180 degrees
common_errors.correct: The interior angles of any triangle in Euclidean geometry always sum to exactly 180 degrees.

common_errors.wrong: vertical angles are adjacent to each other
common_errors.correct: Vertical angles are the non-adjacent angles formed by two intersecting lines, and they are always equal.

common_errors.wrong: alternate interior angles are supplementary
common_errors.correct: Alternate interior angles are EQUAL (congruent) when formed by parallel lines cut by a transversal.

common_errors.wrong: a right triangle can have an obtuse angle
common_errors.correct: A right triangle has one 90-degree angle, and the other two must be acute (less than 90) since they sum to 90.

facts.statement: The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right triangle, a^2 + b^2 = c^2, where c is the hypotenuse
The hypotenuse is the longest side of a right triangle, opposite the right angle
Common Pythagorean triples include (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (8,15,17), and (7,24,25)
The converse of the Pythagorean theorem: if a^2 + b^2 = c^2, then the triangle is a right triangle
Any multiple of a Pythagorean triple is also a Pythagorean triple: (6,8,10) is 2x(3,4,5)
The distance formula d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) is derived from the Pythagorean theorem
In a 45-45-90 triangle, the legs are equal and the hypotenuse = leg x sqrt(2)
In a 30-60-90 triangle, sides are in ratio 1 : sqrt(3) : 2
The midpoint formula: midpoint = ((x1+x2)/2, (y1+y2)/2)

common_errors.wrong: the Pythagorean theorem works for all triangles
common_errors.correct: The Pythagorean theorem only works for right triangles (triangles with one 90-degree angle).

common_errors.wrong: c is always the largest number
common_errors.correct: c must be the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right angle). It is always the longest side of a right triangle.

common_errors.wrong: a^2 + b^2 = c means you just add a and b
common_errors.correct: You must square a and b first, add those squares, then take the square root to find c.

common_errors.wrong: in a 30-60-90 triangle, the sides are 1, 2, 3
common_errors.correct: The sides are in ratio 1 : sqrt(3) : 2, approximately 1 : 1.73 : 2.

common_errors.wrong: the distance between (1,2) and (4,6) is (4-1) + (6-2) = 7
common_errors.correct: Use the distance formula: sqrt((4-1)^2 + (6-2)^2) = sqrt(9+16) = sqrt(25) = 5.

facts.statement: Volume of a rectangular prism = length x width x height
Volume of a cube = side^3 (side cubed)
Volume of a cylinder = pi x r^2 x height
Volume of a sphere = (4/3) x pi x r^3
Volume of a cone = (1/3) x pi x r^2 x height
Volume of a pyramid = (1/3) x base area x height
Surface area of a rectangular prism = 2(lw + lh + wh)
Volume is measured in cubic units (cm^3, m^3, ft^3)
Surface area of a cube = 6 x side^2
Surface area of a cylinder = 2 x pi x r^2 + 2 x pi x r x h
Surface area of a sphere = 4 x pi x r^2
Lateral surface area of a cone = pi x r x slant height
Volume of a triangular prism = (1/2) x base x height of triangle x length of prism
A net is a 2D pattern that can be folded to form a 3D shape

common_errors.wrong: volume of a cone is pi x r^2 x height
common_errors.correct: Volume of a cone is (1/3) x pi x r^2 x height. A cone is one-third of a cylinder with the same base and height.

common_errors.wrong: volume of a sphere is pi x r^3
common_errors.correct: Volume of a sphere is (4/3) x pi x r^3. The coefficient 4/3 must not be omitted.

common_errors.wrong: doubling each dimension doubles the volume
common_errors.correct: Doubling each dimension of a 3D shape multiplies the volume by 8 (2^3), not 2.

common_errors.wrong: surface area and volume use the same units
common_errors.correct: Surface area uses square units (cm^2); volume uses cubic units (cm^3).

common_errors.wrong: a cube has 4 faces
common_errors.correct: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges, and 8 vertices.

facts.statement: A polygon is a closed figure with straight sides; triangles (3), quadrilaterals (4), pentagons (5), hexagons (6)
A regular polygon has all sides equal and all angles equal
Congruent figures have the same shape and size; similar figures have the same shape but may differ in size
An equilateral triangle has three equal sides and three 60-degree angles
An isosceles triangle has at least two equal sides and two equal base angles
A scalene triangle has no equal sides and no equal angles
The sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral is 360 degrees
A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides; opposite sides are equal and opposite angles are equal
A rectangle is a parallelogram with four right angles
A square is a rectangle with four equal sides (also a rhombus with four right angles)
A rhombus has four equal sides; its diagonals bisect each other at right angles
A trapezoid has exactly one pair of parallel sides
The triangle inequality: the sum of any two sides must be greater than the third side
Similar figures have proportional sides and equal corresponding angles; the scale factor relates their sizes
A line of symmetry divides a figure into two mirror-image halves
A heptagon has 7 sides, an octagon has 8, a nonagon has 9, and a decagon has 10

common_errors.wrong: a square is not a rectangle
common_errors.correct: A square IS a special type of rectangle where all four sides are equal. Every square is a rectangle, but not every rectangle is a square.

common_errors.wrong: all quadrilaterals are parallelograms
common_errors.correct: Quadrilaterals include many shapes (trapezoids, kites) that are not parallelograms. A parallelogram is a special quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides.

common_errors.wrong: similar figures are the same size
common_errors.correct: Similar figures have the same shape but may be different sizes. Congruent figures are both the same shape AND size.

common_errors.wrong: a triangle can have sides 2, 3, and 6
common_errors.correct: By the triangle inequality, 2 + 3 = 5, which is NOT greater than 6. These sides cannot form a triangle.

common_errors.wrong: all rhombuses are squares
common_errors.correct: A rhombus has 4 equal sides but does not need right angles. Only rhombuses with 4 right angles are squares.

facts.statement: A translation (slide) moves every point the same distance and direction without rotating or flipping
A reflection (flip) produces a mirror image across a line of reflection
A rotation (turn) turns a figure around a fixed point by a given angle
A dilation changes the size of a figure by a scale factor, keeping the shape the same
Translations, reflections, and rotations are rigid transformations: they preserve size and shape (congruence)
A dilation is NOT a rigid transformation: it preserves shape (similarity) but not size
A 90-degree clockwise rotation of point (x, y) around the origin gives (y, -x)
A 180-degree rotation of point (x, y) around the origin gives (-x, -y)
Reflecting (x, y) over the x-axis gives (x, -y); over the y-axis gives (-x, y)
A scale factor greater than 1 enlarges; between 0 and 1 shrinks; equal to 1 keeps same size

common_errors.wrong: a reflection changes the size of a figure
common_errors.correct: Reflections are rigid transformations that preserve size and shape. Only dilations change size.

common_errors.wrong: rotating 90 degrees clockwise is the same as rotating 90 degrees counterclockwise
common_errors.correct: They produce different results. 90 CW maps (x,y) to (y,-x); 90 CCW maps (x,y) to (-y,x).

common_errors.wrong: dilation always makes figures bigger
common_errors.correct: A scale factor less than 1 (like 0.5) shrinks the figure. Only scale factors greater than 1 enlarge.

common_errors.wrong: after a translation, the figure faces a different direction
common_errors.correct: A translation moves every point equally without rotating. The orientation stays the same.

facts.statement: SOH CAH TOA: sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan = opposite/adjacent
In a right triangle, the side opposite an angle is across from it; the adjacent side is next to it (not the hypotenuse)
sin(45) = cos(45) = sqrt(2)/2 (approximately 0.707)
sin^2(x) + cos^2(x) = 1 for all angles x (Pythagorean identity)
tan(x) = sin(x) / cos(x)
The unit circle has radius 1 centered at the origin; any point on it is (cos(angle), sin(angle))

common_errors.wrong: sin means opposite over adjacent
common_errors.correct: sin = opposite/hypotenuse (SOH). tan = opposite/adjacent (TOA).

common_errors.wrong: sin(30) = sqrt(3)/2
common_errors.correct: sin(30) = 1/2. It is cos(30) that equals sqrt(3)/2.

common_errors.wrong: trig ratios only work in right triangles with the standard right angle
common_errors.correct: Basic SOH CAH TOA works in any right triangle. The right angle can be at any vertex.

common_errors.wrong: sin(2x) = 2 sin(x)
common_errors.correct: sin(2x) = 2 sin(x) cos(x). Trig functions are not linear; you cannot simply multiply the argument.
